slides.title: Universal (Forwarding) References
slides.prompt: A template parameter declared as T&& in a type-deduction context is a universal (forwarding) reference. Depending on whether an lvalue or rvalue is passed, it can collapse to either an lvalue reference or an rvalue reference.

slides.title: Forwarding Reference Syntax Context
slides.prompt: Fill in the auto keyword modifier that creates a universal reference in generic lambda bindings.

slides.title: Reference Collapsing Rules
slides.prompt: According to C++ reference collapsing rules, what does 'T& &&' collapse into?
options: T& (lvalue reference always wins over rvalue reference)
slides.correctAnswer: T& (lvalue reference always wins over rvalue reference)

slides.title: Reference Collapsing Combinations
slides.prompt: Fill in the resulting reference type when collapsing 'T&& &&'.

slides.title: Distinguishing Forwarding Ref from Rvalue Ref
slides.prompt: Why is 'std::vector<T>::push_back(T&&)' NOT a universal (forwarding) reference?
options: Type deduction does not happen for push_back when the class template T is already instantiated
vector elements are stored on heap memory
slides.correctAnswer: Type deduction does not happen for push_back when the class template T is already instantiated
